subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add a core pace-aware provider usage and admission contract for autonomous agents, and what is the minimal first scope?
rationale: The request adds provider-specific usage semantics, persisted runtime state, agent default config, status/session_status output, and possibly autonomous throttling; automation should not choose those defaults or product boundaries.

options.title: Visibility-First Core Pace
options.body: Expose pace projections in status/session_status and agent context first, while leaving automatic throttling disabled until the semantics are proven.

options.title: Opt-In Enforcement Contract
options.body: Add `agents.defaults.pace` with explicit opt-in thresholds and tests for subagent and non-interactive blocking behavior.

options.title: Plugin/Skill Boundary First
options.body: Keep pace projections in `claude-pace` or a plugin, and add only the missing provider usage hook or SDK seam if current extension points cannot support it.

recommendation.title: Visibility-First Core Pace
recommendation.body: Expose pace projections in status/session_status and agent context first, while leaving automatic throttling disabled until the semantics are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is product/config direction across provider usage, agent defaults, and session status, where steipete has the strongest observed adjacent history.
